zakat.claim_evidence: Pillars Fund is a grant-making organization and Muslim community foundation named in reference to the five pillars of Islam, the third of which is Zakat. Pillars is focused on funding secular non-profit programs supporting American Muslims in media, public relations, and leadership development. (Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pillars_Fund)

all_citations.claim: Pillars Fund has a 94.0/100 score, 20.7 months of working capital, a 74.3% program expense ratio, and $0.12 fundraising efficiency.
Total revenue for the organization was $5,966,431 in fiscal year 2024.
Pillars Fund supports nonprofit organizations that amplify the talents of American Muslims.
The organization supports scholarly and creative contributions to the Muslim narrative.
Pillars Fund supports fellows in cohorts to advance their creative work.

baseline_narrative.amal_score_rationale: Pillars Fund is a stable organization with high transparency and clear evidence of its work, though its moderate program spending ratio and focus on long-term cultural change result in an average assessment.
areas_for_improvement: The program expense ratio of 74.3% is moderate, meaning about a quarter of spending goes to overhead and administration [1].
The focus on capacity building and cultural narrative change can make it harder to measure immediate direct impact per dollar compared to emergency aid groups.

dimension_explanations.alignment: This group serves as a bridge for donors interested in American Muslim cultural and religious representation [3]. It has a solid track record of supporting cohorts of artists and leaders [8]. However, the cause is categorized as a religious and cultural area, which some donors may view with less urgency than immediate humanitarian needs [1].
dimension_explanations.impact: The organization focuses on capacity building by investing in fellows and creative contributors to change public narratives [6][8]. It shows moderate spending efficiency with a program expense ratio of 74.3% in FY2024 [1]. While it has strong governance and clear evidence of its outcomes, the nature of its work makes the cost per beneficiary less direct than traditional service charities [1].

strengths_deep_dive: Pillars Fund demonstrates exceptional governance and leadership, evidenced by its <cite id="1">perfect 100/100 Leadership & Adaptability score</cite> from Charity Navigator. The organization has successfully <cite id="4">invested and leveraged $30,000,000</cite> to support Muslim narratives. Its grantmaking is extensive, reaching <cite id="2">111 domestic recipients</cite> with millions in funding. This scale is supported by a <cite id="2">board of 9 members</cite> providing oversight. The organization's ability to maintain <cite id="1">high fundraising efficiency</cite> while growing its revenue base suggests a professionalized operation capable of managing complex cultural initiatives.
rich_narrative.summary: Pillars Fund is a specialized grantmaking institution that works to shift the narrative of American Muslims by <cite id="3">supporting artists and nonprofit leaders</cite>. The organization focuses on capacity building and cultural representation through initiatives like the <cite id="6">Pillars Artist Fellowship and Storytelling Grants</cite>. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="2">total revenue of $5,966,431</cite>, reflecting a multi-year growth trend with a <cite id="2">3-year CAGR of 24.4%</cite>. While the charity maintains a <cite id="1">94/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, its model focuses on long-term cultural change rather than immediate direct aid. This approach results in a <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 74.3%</cite>, which is just below the 75% sector benchmark. Financial management is a notable strength, as the organization holds <cite id="1">20.7 months of working capital</cite> in working capital, ensuring significant stability for its multi-year fellowship commitments. The charity operates as a significant grantmaker, distributing <cite id="2">$6,560,000 in total grants</cite> to 111 recipients in the most recent filing year, including groups like the <cite id="2">Inner City Muslim Action Network</cite>.
